newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Latest wave of Burma refugees leave Bangladesh.
newsitem.headline: Latest wave of Burma refugees leave Bangladesh.

text.p: More than 500 Moslem refugees left for their homes in Burma on Thursday after more than four years in refugee camps in Bangladesh's Cox's Bazar district, officials said.
The latest batch, which comprised 190 families, sailed across the Naf river on the border, the officials said.
After their departure an estimated 26,872 Rohingyas Moslems refugees still remain in Bangladesh.
The refugees are among 250,000 Moslems who fled to southeastern Bangladesh in early 1992 from Burma's Moslem-majority Arakan province, complaining of military persecution.
Repatriation began in September, 1992 following an agreement between Dhaka and Rangoon.
So far 224,000 Rohingyas have been repatriated under supervision of the U.N. High Commisioner for Refugees, officials said.
Officials said early last month that they expected all the refugees to be home by the end of March.
